extracted.intended_audience: high-school students (AP Intro to Public Policy / introductory media studies)
extracted.subtask_short: Intro to Public Policy study guide
extracted.subtask_description: A short, student-facing definition and study aid summarizing Walter Lippmann's contributions to media studies and public opinion for introductory public policy coursework. Includes key facts, review questions, and related concept definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible journalism (objectivity and clarity)
rubrics_metrics.description: He stressed the importance of responsible journalism, arguing that journalists should strive for objectivity and clarity in their reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides evaluation/production of journalism: prioritize factual accuracy, clear presentation, and impartial tone. Rationale given: responsible journalism helps prevent misinformation that can distort public understanding and hinder informed policy discussions. Anti-patterns include sensationalism, partisan framing, and unclear reporting that create confusion or bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media as mediator between public and government
rubrics_metrics.description: The media acts as a mediator between the public and government, shaping perceptions of reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing media or policy communication, consider how news outlets translate events and governmental actions into accessible information for the public. Implication: media selection, emphasis, and simplification influence what the public perceives as the political reality and therefore affect public opinion and policy responsiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agenda-setting (media determines topic importance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lippmann believed that the media has the power to shape the agenda for public discourse, determining what topics are seen as important.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this criterion to judge influence: measure which issues receive coverage and prominence. Guidance: high coverage/foregrounding by media often elevates an issue's public salience and can shift policy priorities. Anti-patterns: ignoring important issues or over-covering trivial ones, which skews public priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stereotypes / simplified images due to informational limits
rubrics_metrics.description: He introduced the idea that people often rely on simplified images or stereotypes when forming opinions about complex social issues due to the limitations of information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments should check for oversimplification: verify whether reporting or policy communication reduces complex topics to stereotypes or facile images. Example effect: simplified representations can produce skewed perceptions that affect policy discussions. Anti-patterns: relying on cliched narratives or one-dimensional portrayals of groups/issues without context or nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media framing (emphasis and omission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Media Framing: The way media presentations influence how audiences interpret events or issues by emphasizing certain aspects while downplaying others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how frames highlight particular causes, actors, or solutions and omit alternatives. Guidance: identify dominant frames and consider alternative framings; framing choices can change public interpretation and policy support. Anti-patterns: single-perspective framing, lack of counterframes, or opaque framing that conceals underlying assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public opinion formation (indirect, media-influenced)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public opinion is not formed solely through direct experience but is significantly influenced by media representations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing public opinion or designing communications, account for mediation effects—how information selection, framing, and simplification by media shape beliefs. Practical implication: to influence or measure public opinion, examine media content and its alignment with lived experience; beware assuming direct experience is the main driver of opinion.
